scenes.contextualRelevance: This scene demonstrates a basic chemical reaction, showing the process of dissolving Sodium Hydroxide Pellets in water and the resulting exothermic reaction.

narrativeProgression.description: The Teacher introduces the experiment, showing a bottle of Sodium Hydroxide Pellets.
He adds a few pellets to a flask.
Water is added to the flask.
The Teacher shakes the flask to dissolve the pellets, explaining that the reaction is exothermic.

Add Phenolphthalein indicator to the flask
Show the flask with pink color
Explain the color change indicates a base
Show the color fading as acid is added
Show the clear solution after neutralization
Add more NaOH to make the solution pink again
Add more HCl to neutralize the solution again

characterInteraction.description: The Teacher interacts with the students, engaging them in the experiment and asking them questions to test their understanding. The students observe the demonstration attentively and respond to the Teacher's questions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: This scene focuses on the concept of neutralization, illustrating how the reaction between an acid and a base results in a neutral solution. The use of Phenolphthalein as an indicator is highlighted, showing its color change in acidic and basic solutions.

narrativeProgression.description: The Teacher shows the flask with fully dissolved Sodium Hydroxide, noting that it's now NaOH solution.
He adds Phenolphthalein indicator to the solution.
The solution turns pink, signifying it's a base.
The Teacher begins adding acid (HCl) to the solution.
The pink color gradually fades as more acid is added, demonstrating neutralization.
The solution becomes completely clear, indicating a neutral pH.
The Teacher explains the concept of neutralization and how the reaction produced salt and water.
To further illustrate the concept, he adds more NaOH, turning the solution pink again.
He then adds HCl again, neutralizing the solution back to a clear state.
